overview.summary: Correct 0.24 execution isolation in four ordered slices: resolve an explicit per-agent boundary, establish a portable scoped host gateway without agent egress, enforce that boundary for Claude and Codex, then close ACP/workflow gaps and reconcile release documentation and conformance evidence.

sharedDecisions.title: Two-axis execution policy
sharedDecisions.description: Execution mode is host or container; a security profile describes only a container filesystem/capability posture. S01 defines the effective policy and worker identity consumed unchanged by S02–S04.

sharedDecisions.title: Conservative resolution and no fallback
sharedDecisions.description: Explicit logical-agent policy wins, identityless tasks may use a task-type fallback, and the deployment default is last. Provider/platform validation follows resolution and rejects every unsupported combination without substituting host execution.

sharedDecisions.title: Separate provider credentials from host capabilities
sharedDecisions.description: S02 supplies one lifecycle and transport boundary, but provider-specific request adapters and principal-scoped MCP authorization remain distinct authorities. No universal destination proxy or shared steward MCP token is exposed.

sharedDecisions.title: Portable no-egress transport
sharedDecisions.description: Every agent container retains Docker network none on Linux and Docker Desktop. S02 uses host-controlled, surface-separated bounded framed pipes over docker exec stdin/stdout; no host socket mount, bridge network, or egress-capable relay is introduced.

sharedDecisions.title: Execution-scoped bridge authority
sharedDecisions.description: Every live container authority owns one container/process namespace, harness lifetime, generated state, and provider/MCP pipe set. Container harnesses never enter the reusable worker cache; release confirms process termination, revokes the pipes/authority, removes generated state, and destroys the container. Reusable provider credentials remain host-only.

sharedDecisions.title: Verified provider authentication only
sharedDecisions.description: Containerized Claude supports host-held ANTHROPIC_API_KEY mediation only; OAuth/setup-token combinations require explicit host execution. Containerized Codex uses an auth-clean home and the documented custom Responses-provider seam. Future providers and ACP registrations must declare a proven mechanism or fail closed.

bindingConstraints.verbatim: A conflict is rejected; it is never silently weakened, strengthened, or substituted.
Container profiles are valid only for container mode.
Provider credentials remain absent from container-visible environment variables, files, arguments, and generated client configuration.
Authorization must be enforced on the host for the effective principal and tool set rather than trusted to client-side tool suppression.
Bridge authorization is bound to one execution principal and lifetime; authorization captured from one agent, session, or worker cannot be replayed by another or after the originating execution ends.

Every live container authority owns one container/process namespace, harness lifetime, bridge pipe set, and generated state; container harnesses are disposed rather than cached across authority release.
Every agent container uses `network:none`; arbitrary direct egress probe fails
Containerized Claude uses host-held `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` mediation without receiving the key; OAuth/setup-token combinations are rejected with deliberate host execution as the supported alternative.

stories.name: Effective execution policy
stories.scope: Add restart-time host/container selection for the primary and logical agents plus identityless task-type fallbacks; resolve one validated policy shared by task, workflow, crash and scheduling paths; separate container profile from execution mode in worker identity, preserve host caching, make each container authority own a non-cached container harness, and amend ADR-012 before gateway work.
stories.notes: The policy value must reach every runner path explicitly; an unknown profile or missing manager cannot continue to mean host execution implicitly. Container-mode reuse ends at authority release; provider capacity accounting remains unchanged.

stories.name: Scoped host gateway
stories.scope: Replace the Anthropic-only socket assumption with one host-owned gateway lifecycle and surface-separated bounded framed stdio pipes over docker exec, while keeping provider request adapters separate from principal-scoped MCP capabilities; bind authorization out of band to the owning container authority and prove framing, backpressure, denied egress, tool access and replay on Linux and Docker Desktop.
stories.notes: The bridge is a small Dart-owned container process with one host-controlled pipe per provider/MCP surface. Raw socat multiplexing, bearer-only identity, network attachment, destination selection, and reusable credentials are forbidden.

stories.name: Claude and Codex container parity
stories.scope: Make long-lived and workflow-owned Claude and Codex honor the effective boundary, route provider traffic through their host-owned adapters, reject Claude OAuth/setup-token container mode, give restricted Codex an auth-clean home and pinned working binary, connect both clients to scoped host MCP, disable unmediated native web fallback, and verify actual placement and secret absence.
stories.notes: Codex must use its documented custom Responses provider through ephemeral launch overrides; do not mount or reuse the host Codex home in container mode.

stories.name: ACP compatibility and release conformance
stories.scope: Declare and validate ACP launch, credential and host-capability compatibility instead of discarding required managers; close standalone/workflow enforcement gaps; add startup diagnostics and the cross-provider success/denial matrix; verify S01's ADR-012 lineage and synchronize architecture, user configuration, agent/task/security guides and 0.24 release notes without changing the memory bundle.
stories.notes: ACP compatibility is declarative and fail-closed; 0.24 does not promise a credential or MCP adapter for arbitrary ACP binaries. Compare the final memory-bundle Git tree object with the pre-S01 object rather than relying only on a clean worktree diff.

riskSummary.mitigation: Exhaustively test precedence, contradictory settings, default preservation, host cache compatibility, container harness disposal and ADR-012 lineage before provider work builds on the policy.
Use bounded surface-separated framed stdio, per-authority container ownership, adversarial framing/replay/tool/egress probes and forced cleanup failures on Linux and Docker Desktop.
Run real placement and request-header tests for both harnesses, inspect all container-visible surfaces for provider secrets, and pin the Codex artifact contract.
Validate each ACP topology and workflow entry point against one conformance matrix, reject undeclared mechanisms, and make release claims only for exercised paths.

executionNotes: Before S01, record the Git tree object for dev/bundle/docs/specs/0.24/. Execute S01 then S02. S03 establishes first-class Claude/Codex behavior on that foundation. S04 is the final compatibility, conformance and documentation gate and must compare that recorded tree object. Any story that cannot preserve network:none, one live authority per container/harness, and host-only reusable credentials must stop with BLOCKED rather than weaken the boundary.
